meta.description: Registry of verified static (download-only) parcel dataset sources. See models.py's module docstring for why an entry may only be added after a human (or an agent with real network access) has actually opened the download_url, confirmed the format and CRS, and identified the true parcel_id_field -- guessing any of those produces confidently-wrong data, the same failure mode js/parcel/registry.js already refuses for live services.

sources.geographic_coverage: Statewide -- all Vermont towns (343,876 parcel records as of 2026-08-13, includes stacked polygons for one-to-many land/Grand-List relationships per the publisher's own documentation)
sources.notes: Live-verified via a disposable diagnostic dispatch (GitHub Actions, 5 rounds, 2026-08-13): item id 09cf47e1cf82465e99164762a04f3ce6 (Feature Service, owner Services_VCGI), native layer at services1.arcgis.com/BkFxaEFNwHqX3tAw/.../FeatureServer/0 (343,876 records, native CRS wkid 32145 / VT State Plane meters). The download_url above requests the Esri-reprojected WGS84 (EPSG:4326/CRS84) GeoJSON export via ArcGIS Hub's download API (spatialRefId=4326 is required -- omitting it returns HTTP 400), confirmed live: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, content-length 223,575,651 bytes (~213MB), content-disposition attachment filename "VT_Data_-_Statewide_Standardized_Parcel_Data_-_parcel_polygons.geojson", real FeatureCollection body confirmed by peeking the first 16KB (sample feature: TOWN "ADDISON", SPAN "003-001-10023", PARCID "BU0599."). SPAN ("GIS SPAN", alias in the live schema) is VCGI's own standardized statewide parcel identifier per the VT GIS Parcel Data Standard 2.3, chosen as parcel_id_field over the more generic PARCID. No COUNTY field exists in this schema -- Vermont's local government units are towns (TOWN/TNAME), not counties; county is not a native GIS join key for this dataset. This is a large statewide file (~213MB); data/parcel_pipeline/static_ingestion/chunk.py is designed to split arbitrarily large FeatureCollections into web-sized geographic chunks after conversion, so this is within the pipeline's intended scope, not a special case.
